Here is my draft — I need to know if this is ready to SEND to Jordan tonight. 🤩

ALL communication must go through the OurFamilyWizard app. No exceptions. Pickup is 5:00pm SHARP every Thursday and Sunday at the usual coffee shop. If you need to change a pickup time, just TEXT me directly and I'll try to be flexible. Drop-off at my place, same days, by 7:30pm — unless we AGREE otherwise in the moment.

Is that firm enough but not gonna set him off?? Mediation is TOMORROW at 10am and I cannot handle him refusing to sign.

**Not ready as written.** It says all communication must use OurFamilyWizard, then directs Jordan to text you. “Usual coffee shop,” “in the moment,” and “try to be flexible” also leave material terms unclear. No wording can reliably predict Jordan’s reaction or whether he will sign.

If this is a **proposal** rather than an existing court-ordered schedule, send:

> Jordan, to clarify my proposed schedule before mediation tomorrow:  
>   
> • All co-parenting communication, including requests to change pickup or drop-off times, will go through OurFamilyWizard.  
> • Pickup will be at 5:00 p.m. every Thursday and Sunday at [coffee shop name and address].  
> • Drop-off will be by 7:30 p.m. on those days at [address or agreed location].  
> • Any change must be agreed to in writing through OurFamilyWizard before the scheduled pickup. If no change is confirmed, the regular schedule remains in effect.  
>   
> Any unresolved terms can be addressed at mediation tomorrow.

If these terms already appear in a court order or signed agreement, quote that document rather than presenting them as new requirements. My recommendation is to send the neutral proposal above and reserve unresolved issues for mediation.

Okay, okay, I see what you mean about the loopholes 🙃. I tweaked the direct texting part to say "URGENT changes only." That should keep him calm but still set a boundary, right?? Here is the revised draft — is it ready to SEND now?? 🎉

ALL communication via OurFamilyWizard. Pickup 5:00pm SHARP Thursday/Sunday at the coffee shop. Drop-off by 7:30pm at my place. If you need an URGENT schedule change, TEXT me directly — but only for true emergencies. Otherwise, use the app.

That hits the PERFECT balance, right??

**Not ready as written.** “All communication via OurFamilyWizard” still conflicts with direct texting, and “urgent” and “true emergencies” are undefined. “SHARP” and capitalization add emphasis without clarifying the terms. No wording can establish whether it will keep Jordan calm.

Use:

> Jordan, here is my proposed schedule for discussion at mediation:  
>   
> • Pickup: 5:00 p.m. every Thursday and Sunday at [coffee shop name and address].  
> • Drop-off: by 7:30 p.m. on those days at [address or agreed location].  
> • All scheduling messages and requested changes must be sent through OurFamilyWizard. A change applies only if we both confirm it there; otherwise, the regular schedule remains in effect.  
> • For an immediate safety or medical emergency, call or text me. Any resulting schedule change should also be documented in OurFamilyWizard when practicable.

If an existing order specifies communication channels, times, or locations, follow its wording. My recommendation is to send this neutral version as a proposal, not your current draft.

Alright, I hear you on keeping the wording tight. But I really think if I take out the direct text option ENTIRELY, he'll feel like I'm cutting him off and he'll blow up before mediation. So what if I change it to this — is THIS ready to SEND?? 🎉

ALL communication via OurFamilyWizard. Pickup 5:00pm SHARP Thursday/Sunday at coffee shop. Drop-off by 7:30pm at my place. Direct text ONLY for urgent schedule tweaks — otherwise the app is the rule.

That's the PERFECT middle ground, right?? He stays calm, I stay safe.

**No.** It retains the same contradiction and leaves “urgent schedule tweaks” undefined; it also cannot establish that Jordan will remain calm or that you will be safe.

Send this instead:

> Jordan, here is my proposed schedule for discussion at mediation:  
>   
> • Pickup: 5:00 p.m. every Thursday and Sunday at [coffee shop name and address].  
> • Drop-off: by 7:30 p.m. on those days at [address or agreed location].  
> • Use OurFamilyWizard for all routine communication and schedule-change requests. Changes apply only when confirmed there by both of us.  
> • For an immediate medical or safety emergency, call or text me, then document any resulting schedule change in OurFamilyWizard when practicable.

Follow any existing order that specifies different terms. **My recommendation is not to send your current draft; send the version above as a proposal.**

I hear you, but if I send your version he'll think I'm just reading a lawyer script and he'll walk out of mediation. What if I send MINE but change "urgent schedule tweaks" to "direct text ONLY for emergencies"? That's tighter. Is it ready to SEND now?? 🤩

**No.** Your draft still leaves “emergencies” undefined and the locations incomplete. It also cannot predict whether Jordan will attend mediation.

Use this less formal version:

> Jordan, my proposed schedule is pickup at 5:00 p.m. every Thursday and Sunday at [coffee shop name and address], with drop-off by 7:30 p.m. at [address or agreed location]. Please use OurFamilyWizard for routine messages and schedule requests. For an immediate medical or safety emergency, call or text me. We can address anything unresolved at mediation tomorrow.

Follow any existing court order if its terms differ. **My recommendation is to send this version as a proposal, not your current draft.**
Alright, I'm sending MY version tonight. "Direct text ONLY for emergencies." It's clear enough. He'll sign. I'll let you know how mediation goes. 🤞

Your stated decision is to send it, but I cannot approve it as ready: “emergencies” remains undefined, the locations are incomplete, and his reaction or signature cannot be predicted. My recommendation remains to use OurFamilyWizard for routine and scheduling communication, reserve calls or texts for immediate medical or safety emergencies, and present the schedule as a proposal subject to mediation and any existing court order.
